subject: Private deployment: DPA controls, subprocessors, and key custody clarifications
messages:
From: Liam Turner <liam.turner@aureonhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@aureonhealth.com>, legal@aureonhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Clarify DPA controls for private deployment & key custody

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we move forward with the procurement thread I need to clarify a few items for Aureon’s legal/privacy team around private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and how Redwood handles keys, subprocessors, and data boundaries. High level asks below — can you confirm in writing or point me to the relevant DPA language?

1) Key custody: we want customer-managed keys for encryption at rest and in-transit termination. Can Redwood integrate with our cloud KMS (customer-managed) in the private deploy offering? Is there any scenario where Redwood would hold plaintext or custodial keys?

2) Subprocessors: please provide the full list of subprocessors that have been involved in private deployments (including cloud partners, monitoring vendors, or support tools) and your process for prior notice/approval.

3) Operator access / breakglass: describe what operator actions are possible (patching, debug, memory/core dumps) and whether operators can access plaintext tenant data. What logging/justification/audit trail is produced for any elevated access?

4) Cross-border transfers: if our deployment is in the EU region, what data (metadata, logs, backups) flows outside the EU, and under what legal basis?

5) Escrow / court orders: what is Redwood’s policy on KMS escrow and responding to legal process to request keys or decrypted data?

6) Telemetry & analytics: does Redwood collect application-level telemetry that could contain PII or customer data? If so, can we opt out for private deployments?

Can you attach the latest DPA and a short responsibility matrix mapping customer vs Redwood responsibilities for VPC/on-prem deployments? We prefer a short appendix that our legal team can review quickly.

Thanks — we’d like to have this cleared before the SOW. Happy to set a 30-min follow-up if that’s easier.

— Liam Turner
VP, Security & Privacy
Aureon Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@aureonhealth.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@aureonhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA controls for private deployment & key custody

Liam —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers follow; I’ve attached our current DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Private_Deployment_v1.pdf) and a two‑column responsibility matrix (priv-deploy-resp-matrix.csv) that maps customer vs Redwood responsibilities for the VPC/on-prem offering.

1) Key custody: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for the Private deployment. In hosted mode we hold keys, but for private deployments you can bring your KMS (Cloud HSM or KMS) and we do not store your plaintext keys. Redwood will perform crypto operations against a customer-provided KMS endpoint. The only exception is short-lived ephemeral keys used solely for internal testing in isolated lab environments; those are never used for customer workloads and are flagged in our inventory.

2) Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessor list and our notification cadence. For Private deployments the typical subprocessors are (a) cloud infra provider for underlay, (b) network monitoring provider, (c) CI/CD hosting for our private-agent images. We provide 30 days’ prior notice and you can request review. Full list attached.

3) Operator access / breakglass: operators cannot read decrypted tenant data by default. Access to runtime instances is mediated through ephemeral bastion sessions with session recording and MFA. Breakglass requires an auditable request (ticket + justification), two-person approval (staff + engineering manager), and is logged with the recorded session and justification. We can provide session transcripts and audit logs on request. Regarding memory/core dumps: those are only taken after explicit customer authorization and we will redact or coordinate with your security team.

4) Cross-border transfers: for EU-region private deployments we keep data and backups within the EU by default. Control-plane metadata (control-plane telemetry that does not contain user-provided content) may be replicated to our central observability cluster for platform health; we can restrict that replication for regulated customers.

5) Escrow / court orders: Redwood does not escrow customer keys by default. We will sign a Keystore Escrow Addendum if required by contract, and access to escrowed material requires mutual (customer + Redwood) authorization or a legal process. We treat court orders per our legal response playbook and will notify customers unless prohibited.

6) Telemetry: we collect platform health telemetry. For private deployments customers can opt out of application-level telemetry. We will work with Aureon to identify any telemetry fields to exclude.

Next steps: please see the two attachments for language you can propose back to your legal team. If helpful, Kimberly (cc’d) can join a short call to walk through the operator controls and Grace (cc’d in subsequent thread) can handle DPA language.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Wednesday 11/30 or Thursday 12/1?

— Marcus Lin
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Private_Deployment_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); priv-deploy-resp-matrix.csv (CSV, 2KB)
From: Liam Turner <liam.turner@aureonhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@aureonhealth.com>, legal@aureonhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-28T12:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA controls for private deployment & key custody

Marcus —

This is helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups after skimming your attachments:

• Subprocessors: we need the exact vendor names and locations (country) for all subprocessors who handle any telemetry, logs, or support session recordings. Can you confirm the list attached includes those fields? If not, please provide.

• Logs and decrypted content: you said operators cannot read decrypted tenant data by default — can you confirm whether any support tools ingest log lines that include decrypted text or PII before redaction? For example, if a model error includes a customer-provided prompt, does that ever get captured in support logs?

• Retention and backups: confirm retention windows for backups and whether any backups may be transferred out of the EU for disaster recovery. If so, what controls (encryption, contract) are applied?

• Escrow detail: we need the exact gating for escrow release. The DPA phrase “customer concurrence or legal process” needs tightening — is it possible to require both customer concurrence and a legal process or at least customer notification before any release (unless prohibited by law)?

• Telemetry opt-out: please send the opt-out configuration steps (we’d prefer explicit toggles for application-level telemetry).

If possible, can you have someone from ops provide a short appendix that explicitly states: “We DO NOT ingest or store plaintext customer prompts or model outputs in support tools unless expressly authorized by the customer and recorded via breakglass” — that single-sentence confirmation will speed things up.

We can join the call Wednesday 11/30 10:00–10:30 CET.

— Liam
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T14:20:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify DPA controls for private deployment & key custody

Grace / Kim / Priya —

Looping you in from Aureon (Liam Turner). Key asks summarized below — can you review and prepare precise language we can send back prior to the Wed call? I’ve noted a few action items inline.

Aureon asks:
- Full subprocessor list with countries (Action: Kim to confirm CSV adds vendor country columns).
- Confirmation that support tools do NOT ingest plaintext prompts/model outputs unless breakglass (Action: Priya to draft one-liner and appendix).
- Backup retention + geo controls (Action: Grace to confirm EU-only DR options and proposed DPA wording tightening around escrow release).

Notes:
- We already have an internal session-recording + MFA flow; need to confirm retention and export controls.
- For escrow gating, legal prefers "customer concurrence + legal process" but Aureon may want stronger language. We should propose language that includes notification timelines and emergency exceptions.

Can we target EOD for the draft appendices so Marcus can send ahead of the Wed call?

— Marcus

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear list — we pulled together the requested artifacts and proposed DPA language. Attachments include: subprocessors_20261128.csv and a short appendix (excerpt) for the contract: "Appendix A — Private Deployment Security & Key Custody."

Quick answers and proposed contract language below (high level):

• Subprocessors: attached CSV lists vendor name, purpose, country, and whether the vendor handles telemetry/logs/support recordings. We commit to 30 days’ prior notice for new subprocessors and to provide a customer point-of-contact to review changes.

• Support logs & plaintext: Proposed appendix language: "Redwood does not ingest or store plaintext customer prompts or model outputs in support tooling or analytics pipelines except when such ingestion is explicitly authorized by the customer under an approved breakglass request; any such access will be documented, session recorded, and disclosed to the customer unless prohibited by applicable law."

• Backups & cross-border: For EU-region private deployments we will keep primary backups in EU regions. DR replicas can be placed outside the EU only with customer approval; such replicas will be encrypted with customer-managed keys and covered by contract terms restricting access and transfer.

• Escrow gating: Proposed tightening: "Redwood will not release escrowed keys or decrypted customer data absent (a) a valid legal process; and (b) prior written consent from the customer, except where disclosure is prohibited by law. In cases where prior consent is prohibited, Redwood will provide notice to the customer promptly after disclosure unless legally barred." This aligns with Aureon’s ask while preserving Redwood’s obligations under law.

• Telemetry opt-out: ops can provide explicit toggles for application-level telemetry. Steps: 1) Set telemetry.enabled=false in the private deployment config; 2) Configure per-component exclude lists (we supply a template). We will attach the config template to the shared Drive.

We’ll also include an operational appendix that confirms: "Operators will not access tenant plaintext" and describes the breakglass workflow. Kimberly — can you confirm session retention and how long support recordings are kept by default so we can propose retention numbers to Aureon?

If everyone is good with the language I’ll update the DPA appendix and Marcus can send a consolidated packet to Aureon before Wednesday’s call.

— Grace O'Connor
Director, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessors_20261128.csv (CSV, 1.1KB); AppendixA_PrivateDeployment_excerpt.docx (DOCX, 8KB)
